title: Internal load-balancer Terraform module: multi-mode NLB/ALB, TLS termination, and robust health checks
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Implement a production-ready Terraform module to provision internal-only load balancing for Private (VPC) deployments that supports both NLB and ALB variants, optional TLS termination, comprehensive health checks, and safe upgrade semantics. The module must be reusable across customer VPCs, support pinned subnets/security groups, emit well-defined outputs for downstream modules, and include an upgrade/migration plan to avoid downtime during module version bumps.

Scope and requirements:
- Multi-mode support: variable 'mode' = "nlb" | "alb". Default should be "nlb" for lowest latency and L4 passthrough use-cases, but ALB mode required for path-based routing and host-based rules.
- Internal-only: create LBs in private subnets and set internal flag. Enforce that the module refuses to create internet-facing LBs unless explicitly overridden via an allow_internet_facing boolean (default false).
- TLS termination options: 
  * tls_mode = "none" | "terminate" | "passthrough".
  * terminate: accept cert_arn (ACM) for ALB/NLB TLS listeners. For NLB termination, prefer ACM import for NLB TLS listener where supported; otherwise document KMS/HSM-dependent cert handling.
  * passthrough: configure TCP listeners without termination and pass TLS to backend.
- Health checks: configurable health check type and path. Defaults: ALB -> HTTP path "/healthz" 200; NLB -> TCP port check. Expose health_check_interval, healthy_threshold, unhealthy_threshold, timeout as module inputs.
- Outputs: lb_dns_name, lb_arn, listener_arns, target_group_arns, security_group_ids, subnet_ids, mode, tls_mode.
- IAM/permissions: document minimal IAM needed for Terraform to provision LBs and attach target groups in provider accounts.
- Security posture: tighten security groups to only allow traffic from expected CIDR ranges within VPC and from Redwood-managed NAT/egress where applicable. Default to deny-all except targets and management CIDRs.
- Tagging and ownership: accept map tags and default to {project = "private-deploy", owner = "infra-team"}.
- Lifecycle/upgrades: create_before_destroy semantics for listener and target_group swaps where possible. Provide explicit migration guidance to create new target groups and switch listeners in a non-blocking manner to prevent 503 storms.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Why support both NLB & ALB? We need L4 performance and TLS passthrough for low-latency inference traffic (NLB) while supporting L7 routing (ALB) for console/ops endpoints and webhook-style paths. Supporting both in one module reduces duplication but increases conditional complexity — we will keep common resources minimal and branch for listener/target_group resources.
- TLS handling complexities: ACM integration is easiest for ALB; NLB TLS termination has limitations (ALB supports SNI and advanced policies). For NLB termination we will prefer customer-provided cert_arn; for passthrough document external cert rotation.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before Done):
- Terraform module added under infra/modules/internal-lb and published with a semver tag.
- Module works end-to-end in sandbox account (provisioned via CI) in both modes (nlb and alb) and with tls_mode terminate and passthrough.
- Health check config causes backend targets to be marked healthy/unhealthy correctly in tests.
- Module emits outputs consumed by upstream 'service' modules (target group ARNs, listener ARNs, DNS).
- Upgrade path tested: simulate module version bump and demonstrate zero-downtime cutover in a canary sandbox using create_before_destroy and staged listener swap.
- Terraform plan/apply reviewed and approved in PR with automated plan checks.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests with tfvalidate/tflint.
- Integration tests using Terratest in a dedicated sandbox account: provision sample service, run synthetic traffic and verify 99x success before and after a module upgrade.
- Health-check fuzz tests: change backend container to return 500 and verify unhealthy count triggers alarm and upstream retries.

Rollout and rollout safety:
- Publish module as v0.3.0 in the modules registry.
- For existing customers, provide a migration script (terraform import hints + step-by-step: create new target group, attach, wait for healthy, swap listener target group, destroy old tg).
- Add feature flags for experimental ALB use to avoid accidental flips.

Observability and alerts:
- Create CloudWatch metrics/alarms for UnhealthyHostCount, TargetResponseTime, HTTPCode_Backend_5XX, and Stream-healthy-threshold breaches.
- Integrate LB metrics into Redwood Console dashboards (per-customer) via export hooks; include a dashboard template in docs.

Docs and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Internal+LB+Module (link to be updated with final diagrams).
- Terraform module README with examples for: NLB passthrough, NLB TLS terminate, ALB HTTP/HTTPS path-based routing, and canary upgrade procedure.

Open questions:
- Do we need to support cross-zone load-balancing toggles per-customer? (initial implementation will expose cross_zone_boolean but default true).
- Certificate rotation strategy for NLB-terminated certs in private deployments when ACM in customer account is not available. Work with Security for a recommended flow.
